headline: Indian markets open cautious amid foreign fund outflows, falling crude oil prices, and upcoming IPO DRHP filings.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Sustained FII outflows and global interest rate hike concerns have weighed on benchmark indices.
Crude oil prices fell below $100 per barrel as supply flows recovered, though shortages persist.
Asian markets opened mixed as investors remain on edge over bond yields and global cues.
Government reduced windfall taxes on diesel and ATF exports, keeping petrol duties unchanged.
whatHappening: Indian benchmark indices recorded their worst monthly performance since March.
Over 50 companies filed draft red herring prospectuses (DRHPs) ahead of SEBI's deadline.
Hospital stocks faced downward pressure following Supreme Court inquiries into steep cancer drug markups.
SEBI announced direct money refunds to investors for the first time in the Growpital case.
summary:
Indian equities enter October after logging their worst month since March, impacted by foreign fund outflows and crude oil volatility.
Key developments include a government cut in windfall tax on diesel and ATF exports, along with a rush of DRHP filings ahead of SEBI deadlines.
Traders are watching key stocks like Infosys, HDFC Bank, and Jio Financial alongside global bond yields and Asian market cues.
